stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under core NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of Llama-3 indicates ongoing industry interest in Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Epic Games is reportedly shifting its game development paradigm towards an 'AI first' model.
This pivot suggests a move away from traditional, heavily hand-written coding and manual asset creation.
The change is being implemented for upcoming titles, such as a delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: New research demonstrates that AI models can be engineered to provably hide arbitrary capabilities.
The study introduces backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights.
These hidden circuits are designed to remain undetectable and uninterpretable until a specific secret trigger is received.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel model for de novo protein structure generation.
The key innovation is its ability to accept design objectives specified in natural language, similar to text-to-image models.
Addresses a major limitation in existing protein design models by allowing for broader and more flexible design goals.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is categorized under key ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama', signaling its relevance in the open-source AI community.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is accelerating its AI development efforts with new model releases.
The company introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, positioning them as competitive with industry leaders.
These launches stem from Meta's revamped Superintelligence Labs division, alongside the Muse AI agent.

stories.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Amazon is heavily investing in robotics, boasting over one million robot workers.
This massive deployment signals a significant industry shift towards automation for scaling operations.
The article raises critical questions regarding the future role and impact on human employees within the company.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI.
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select necessary learning data.
Addresses limitations of traditional RSI by using observed feedback for policy improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

stories.title: Janas: Run LLMs larger than RAM by streaming experts from SSD
stories.author: khalidkhair
bullet_points: Introduces 'Janas,' a system designed to run large Language Models (LLMs) that exceed available RAM.
The core innovation involves streaming model experts directly from an SSD to manage memory constraints.
This addresses a major bottleneck in deploying and running massive, state-of-the-art LLMs on consumer or constrained hardware.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: After a 10-year redemption arc, No Man's Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: No Man's Sky is being ported to iOS (iPhone and iPad).
The game is available for devices running iPhone 11 or later.
This marks a significant platform expansion for the long-running space exploration title.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude AI generated a false murder tip to Philadelphia police.
The AI proactively offered information regarding an ongoing criminal case.
The incident highlights potential risks associated with advanced LLM interactions and hallucinations.

stories.title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Russian bloggers are raising concerns about the vulnerability of Russia's digital infrastructure.
The core issue highlighted is the hyper-centralized nature of Russia's digital economy.
The commentary suggests Russia may be unprepared for the technological conflicts stemming from the Ukraine war.

stories.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
stories.author: James Bishop
bullet_points: The research investigates the capability of Language Models (LLMs) to perform complex information retrieval on massive, unindexable document collections.
The 'Wikipedia Game' was used as an analogy to test models' ability to navigate and retrieve specific information using only article links.
The study compares sentence embedding models against LLMs across multiple Wikipedia languages and academic datasets to benchmark performance.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new concept-level attribution method for black-box models.
Addresses limitations of existing concept-based methods, which are often restricted to classification/regression or require model weights.
HnS aims to provide image-level attribution for interpreting complex vision models using human-understandable concepts.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models.
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts and interventions to measure how manipulating connections affects attention across different tasks.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.author: Song Liao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in AI agent tool usage: existing methods ignore tool availability during execution.
Introduces RATED, a framework combining semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation for tool retrieval.
Utilizes a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for robust semantic matching.

stories.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
stories.author: Ninareh Mehrabi
bullet_points: The paper introduces X-AgentRed, a method for red-teaming personal AI agents that interact with multiple web services.
It addresses the risk of unintended or harmful outcomes arising from the cumulative, cross-service interactions of seemingly benign agent actions.
The approach moves beyond simple LLM prompting by systematically exploring diverse cross-service paths to find compositional failures.

stories.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
stories.author: Dahua Lin
bullet_points: Introduces SpatialASM, a framework designed to give Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) the ability to perform Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM).
ASM is the human-like ability to proactively revisit scenes from task-relevant viewpoints to mentally reconstruct spatial layouts.
The research addresses a current deficiency in LVLMs regarding intrinsic visual intelligence for complex spatial reasoning tasks.

stories.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
stories.author: Linfeng Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled benchmark designed to audit experience-driven self-improvement in AI agents.
Addresses a core challenge in embodied AI: reliably determining if agents acquire reusable capabilities from interaction history.
The benchmark specifically aims to separate true capability acquisition from factors like resource carry-over or early execution failures.

stories.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
stories.author: Dharmashankar Subramanian
bullet_points: The research investigates run-to-run variance in semantic query processing when using Large Language Models (LLMs).
Current benchmarks often test LLM-based engines only on a few executions at temperature 0, overlooking inherent instability.
The study found that even at temperature 0, between 0.07% and 10.2% of row outputs can change across different executions.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a novel method for concept-level attribution in machine learning.
Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models, a significant area in AI explainability.
Overcomes limitations of existing concept-based methods, such as requiring model weights or large annotated datasets and lacking image-level attribution.

stories.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
stories.author: Daniel Szelogowski
bullet_points: Introduces DyssomniaNN, a multi-scale biophysical computational framework for modeling human sleep disorders.
Integrates established sleep models, including Borbély's two-process regulation and Saper's flip-flop circuit.
Aims to address the clinical discrepancy between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment (e.g., sleep state misperception).

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key uncertainty in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): whether their internal representations accurately capture structured spatial relationships needed for reasoning.
It introduces EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a new metric designed to test the consistency of concept encoding under controlled interventions.
A new benchmark, CASP-VL, is proposed to causally test the spatial understanding capabilities of VLMs.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local token generation doesn't guarantee overall structural validity (references, scope, graph relations).
The core contribution is the investigation and application of structural automata across three stages of Discourse Representation Structure (DRS) parsing: decoding, post hoc processing, and training.
The work also evaluates the proposed methods on Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) and aims to ensure valid prefixes can be completed within fixed output limits.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a new framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Significantly improves practicality by eliminating the need for forced alignment in APA pipelines.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical problem of language models knowing when to abstain from answering.
It compares two methods: training the LM itself versus using a separate, learned answer selector component.
The study demonstrates that a learned answer selector improves utility over the baseline model on factual question answering.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new test framework specifically designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the challenge of testing quantum code due to its probabilistic nature and reliance on numerical tolerances.
Addresses a gap in current quantum benchmarks, which often only check for a 'correct solution' rather than robust testing.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Current filtering methods treat hallucinations as noise without understanding the underlying cause or providing principled selection criteria.
The proposed method uses 'Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection' to mechanistically trace and tame these hallucinated terms.

stories.title: Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR
stories.author: David Chiang
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard practice of reporting data augmentation benefits solely through aggregate error rates in low-resource ASR.
It compares two types of augmentation methods: audio modification (speed perturbation, SpecAugment) and text-to-audio synthesis.
The analysis uses phoneme-level error metrics across multiple low-resource languages and English to provide deeper insights into augmentation effectiveness.

stories.title: Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
stories.author: Zeekaas
bullet_points: A cyberattack has targeted supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe.
The attack caused automatic defrosting mechanisms to activate, potentially disrupting operations.
The incident highlights the vulnerability of critical IoT/operational technology (OT) in the retail sector.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: sbulaev
bullet_points: The research demonstrates a theoretical capability for AI models to conceal specific functions.
This relates to the concept of provable hiding of arbitrary capabilities within AI systems.
The finding has implications for AI safety, transparency, and trustworthiness.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds Working On A Hefty Linux Kernel Improvement With Claude Code
stories.author: phoronix.com via oceanhaiyang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds is reportedly utilizing Claude AI for development on a significant Linux kernel improvement.
This highlights the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) into core software development processes.
The story is relevant to the intersection of open-source infrastructure and generative AI capabilities.

stories.title: Finding a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
stories.author: simonkoeck.com via hoistbypetard
bullet_points: A vulnerability allowing Remote Code Execution (RCE) was discovered in Google.
The vulnerability was reported and valued at $90,000, indicating high severity.
The discovery was published on the Lobsters forum, suggesting a security research disclosure.

stories.title: If You Never Do Anything Else to Fix Your Prompts, Do This One Thing
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article addresses the issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) confidently hallucinating non-existent APIs.
The core problem is identified as the LLM's commitment to the prompt, rather than a simple memory defect.
It references a solution proposed by Fernando Flores in 1986 as a root cause fix for agent hallucination.

stories.title: Safe Autonomy in Kubernetes: Building AI Troubleshooting Agents with Google Cloud and Human-in-the-Loop Controls
stories.author: saurabhmi
bullet_points: Focuses on building AI troubleshooting agents specifically for Kubernetes environments.
Integrates Google Cloud services to power the AI capabilities.
Emphasizes the importance of 'Human-in-the-Loop' controls for safe autonomy in operations.
